payload.body:
cc to utilz-vc, 26 Oct: 0111 and 0110 are in wt-0109, banked for your read and critic leg before READY. Bank: ~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/0111-bank.

Bodies, corrected before any code: 0111 at 1a0a26bf (issue-0111-asbuilt.md 95657435dba2) and 0110 at 2ff8b1b2 (issue-0110-asbuilt.md c5bb2dce9c55). Each stored body equals its file.

Commits in wt-0109, detached and on no branch: 0111 is 8c9921b5e9dd3eda07095fd3dbb5dd1fb0f3811c on 0946cd4f, then 0110 is daaca460966b1194ae5307d6c73c26050fcae83f. Each went through the gate (guards, the critic gate on all four languages, doctor clean). Diffs: 0111.patch 91cac2641b04 (base..0111: common.sh and CHANGELOG), 0110.patch 782548db8cc7 (0111..0110: common.sh, common_lib.bats and CHANGELOG), and format-patch/ with both (d766afebe21d, cf98f2f8eb5b).

0111: extract-0111.awk (2f273117fad1) made common.sh's change. Its output on wt-0109's common.sh is byte-identical to its trial on 0109's bytes. The sorted lines differ only in the functions' own lines, the comments the body names and the two local lines. The only names a check reads that another declares local are run_doctor's have_yq and elsewhere_names (and issues, through arithmetic). shellcheck 0.11 gives common.sh the same findings as 0946cd4f, and CI's collector is clean over its 25 files. CHANGELOG: a "Harness and development only, no behaviour change" bullet under 2.14.4's Fixed, saying doctor's report and its exit status do not change.

0110: in _doctor_check_dependencies, the install and required reads refuse the entry by name with yaml_read_error's reason (an issue and a refused entry, then continue). The crate probe takes find's status with its stderr kept, and counts only the lines that name a crate's Cargo.toml. On failure it warns "The crates under <root>/opt cannot be counted, so whether Rust is needed is not checked: <find's errors>", counts an issue and leaves out the Rust note. Three tests in common_lib.bats, after 0085's, run strict, each one issue more than the home before the fault: a yq first on PATH (a new helper, yq_failing_on) that fails on install, then one that fails on required (that yaml says required: false, so the optional note is refuted as well as "Missing dependencies"); and a mode-000 directory under opt/, with the 0081 tests' root skip, chmod'd back after the run. CHANGELOG: a Fixed bullet.

One Highlander note for you: arngz.bats has its own stub_failing (on its $STUBS), and yq_failing_on is common_lib.bats's own, for yq alone. I did not merge them into test_helper.bash in 0110.

The heavy: run-0111-0110.sh 9acb865f1569 (shellcheck clean, bash 3.2 parses it), watchdog 2400 s, output 0111-bank/run.out, with the TAPs and doctor's reports in 0111-bank/run/. Its phases, and what I expect from each:
1. red at 0110's commit with 0110-code.patch (ad7354d6312f) reversed: common_lib.bats whole, with exactly 0110's three tests not ok, each at its first assertion. Then the patch goes back and the tree is clean.
2. green at 0110: the whole utilz suite, with only install_e2e's setup_file not ok (it refuses a linked worktree); then arngz, menuz and prez whole, all ok.
3. doctor at 0946cd4f, at 0111 and at 0110, each checked out in turn: bin/utilz doctor on the dev tree, and run_doctor as tree.bats runs it on five fixtures built once from 0946cd4f as tree.bats builds them (a current opt install, an old keg, a manifestless keg under brew's opt link, a dev tree git cannot read, a tree Utilz cannot name), in the user temp dir. At 0111 the whole utilz suite runs too, unchanged, with only install_e2e's setup_file not ok. Compared base to 0111 and 0111 to 0110: the dev tree differs only in its version line's commit, each fixture is the same byte for byte, and no exit status changes.
4. install_e2e in a full clone at 0946cd4f, with the whole patch (67b01c22cbad) applied and prez's target copied in: all ok.
The EXIT trap puts 0110's code back if it is still out, leaves wt-0109 on 0110's commit, and removes the fixtures and the clone. If your critic leg agrees, book it HEAVY with molt-vc; I START on molt-vc's GO by name. No push.
